initial.title: C-SDLC editor cannot correct SIP scope after implemented review finding
initial.goal: Provide one audited typed route to correct SIP declared scope after implementation and before publication without weakening card or lifecycle authority.
initial.required_outcome: A dedicated csdlc-edit operation corrects implemented-phase SIP declared_scope only when review/publication truth is clear, records the old and new scope plus reason, preserves typed card invariants, and remains unavailable after publication without typed recovery.
authority_boundary: Issue and code authority are agent-logic/agent-design-language#63
Only the typed csdlc-edit semantic operation may correct implemented SIP declared_scope
Canonical values JSON and the markdown.rs-backed renderer remain card truth; Markdown is never mutated directly
csdlc-review remains the sole authority for clearing review and publication truth during recovery
operator_constraints: Never write tracked issue work on main
Use the independent Rust C-SDLC v2 binaries and typed editor route
Require an actor and human reason and retain full previous and replacement scope arrays in audit truth
Use focused deterministic repository-local proof; do not run broad test suites
Do not mutate issue #53 or historical lifecycle evidence
initial.task_boundary: Add an exact implemented-phase SIP declared_scope correction operation and focused invariant proof; do not broaden implemented-phase planning authority or redesign recovery.
deliverables: Exact implemented/SIP/cleared-truth authorization and actor/reason guards
Audit operation retaining previous and replacement scope
Focused real-editor and validator regression coverage
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: The typed editor accepts a nonempty SIP declared_scope correction in implemented phase and advances generation/digest exactly once
AC-2: The audit records actor, reason, complete previous scope, and complete replacement scope
AC-3: Stale generation/digest, empty actor/reason/scope, wrong card, and non-implemented phases fail without mutation
AC-4: Reviewed, published, merge-ready, or retained review/publication/readiness truth rejects correction; a typed recovery to clean implemented state permits it
AC-5: Values JSON, rendered Markdown, cross-card identity, and validator invariants remain coherent; direct Markdown drift remains rejected
AC-6: Focused Rust tests, strict focused Clippy, diff hygiene, and exact-head independent review pass
dependencies: Existing store optimistic concurrency, audit, render, and atomic commit path
non_goals: Automatic semantic classification of scope widening
initial.plan_summary: Freeze the narrow operation and authorization contract, implement through the existing typed AST/render/atomic-commit pipeline, prove accepted correction and all adjacent fail-closed states, validate narrowly, resolve exact-head review, and publish a qualified closing PR.

steps.action: Confirm the dedicated operation, exact phase/card/truth guards, and old/new audit contract.
Implement the semantic operation and store authorization through the existing typed AST, render, validation, and atomic commit path.
Add focused real-editor regressions for accepted correction, exact audit, stale input, adjacent phases/cards, recovery, and projection drift.
Run focused validation and exact-head review, resolve findings, publish, shepherd, and finish truthfully.

invariants: Only SIP declared_scope changes through the new operation
No correction occurs with stale concurrency input or retained review/publication/readiness truth
Every correction exposes its actor, reason, previous scope, and replacement scope in canonical audit truth
Values and rendered Markdown remain generated and cross-card coherent
Normal planning edits and recovery authority remain unchanged
risks: An overly broad match could authorize adjacent implemented-phase SIP fields
Phase-only authorization could permit mutation while stale review or publication evidence remains
Generic audit serialization would omit the previous scope
A test that calls only a helper could miss real csdlc-edit and validator behavior
stop_conditions: The route requires direct Markdown or raw record mutation
Review/publication truth must be cleared by this editor rather than typed recovery
Scope expands beyond the two production modules and focused existing regression surface
Old/new scope and reason cannot be retained atomically

validation_lanes.proof_role: Exercise the real typed editor/store/renderer/validator path for accepted correction, audit truth, concurrency, phase/card guards, recovery, and projection drift.
Reject Rust type, match exhaustiveness, and editor binary regressions on the bounded library and csdlc-edit target.
Reject malformed whitespace and patch artifacts before exact-head review.

initial.failure_policy: Fail closed on stale concurrency truth, empty justification, wrong card or phase, retained review/publication/readiness truth, audit omission, direct Markdown drift, or validator failure.
review_prompts: Can any implemented-phase SIP field other than declared_scope be changed through this route?
Can correction occur while review, publication, or readiness truth remains attached?
Does the audit retain exact previous and replacement arrays plus actor and reason?
Do real editor and validator tests prove rendered-card and stale-input behavior?
Does post-publication recovery remain owned by csdlc-review rather than this operation?
initial.review_scope: Issue 63 design, exact semantic-operation boundary, phase/card/recovery authorization, audit old/new truth, AST/render/validator invariants, focused proof, and no-widening constraints.
